notes.text: Trevor van Riemsdyk is day to day (lower body injury) and has missed the last 11 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Spencer Stastney has taken his spot beside Kris Letang. That pair has had 67% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 60:11 together, up from 39% with van Riemsdyk.

Elmer Söderblom is out week to week (upper body injury) and has missed the last 4 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Nick Robertson has taken his spot beside Connor Dewar and Blake Lizotte. That line has had 58% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 36:00 together.

Bryan Rust is on injured reserve and has missed the last 6 games. Tommy Novak has taken his spot beside Sidney Crosby and Rickard Rakell. That line has had 58% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 66:42 together, up from 43% with Rust.
Ilya Solovyov has started killing penalties: on the ice for 43% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, up from 5% last season.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 31% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 8th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 39%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Troy Terry is on long-term injured reserve (hip surgery) and has missed the last 8 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
A.J. Greer is on injured reserve (upper body injury) and has missed the last 3 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Nico Myatovic has taken his spot beside Sam Colangelo and Tim Washe.
Tyson Hinds has not dressed for the last 4 games. Pavel Mintyukov has taken his spot beside Tristan Luneau.
Laurent Brossoit was added to the roster on Nov 3.
Nico Myatovic was added to the roster on Nov 3 and has played beside Sam Colangelo and Tim Washe.

story.head: The Ducks are rolling
paras: The Ducks have won four straight, while the Penguins are winless in four (0-3-1). The Penguins played last night, and the Ducks are rested. Going in, the Pens are seventh in the Metropolitan (tied for 28th in the NHL) and the Ducks fourth in the Pacific (tied for 14th).

The Penguins have played better than their record (.375) says: their chances are worth about .560, mostly because they’re 3-6 in one-goal games. The Ducks’ record (.559) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.485), largely thanks to their finishing.

The Penguins sit back rather than chase on the forecheck (lowest) and get more of their shots from in close than anyone (1st). They also rarely throw hits (lowest), so the Ducks hit a lot, but them mostly don’t. Pittsburgh has allowed 3.56 goals a game, the fourth most in the league. The Ducks are one of the league’s most physical teams (2nd) and have had shaky goaltending (30th). They also give up a lot of dangerous shots (30th), so the Penguins could find some good looks against them, who give up plenty of them. Anaheim has scored 3.76 goals a game, the fourth most in the league, and allowed 3.76, the third most.

Erik Karlsson (3 G / 13 A / 16 P in 16 GP) leads the Penguins in scoring, and Nick Robertson (7 G / 0 A / 7 P in 16 GP) has a team-high seven goals. Leo Carlsson (6 G / 20 A / 26 P in 17 GP) leads the Ducks in scoring and is tied for sixth in the NHL, with eleven points in his last five games. Cutter Gauthier (12 G / 6 A / 18 P in 16 GP) has a team-high twelve goals, tied for fourth in the NHL, with eleven points in his last five games.

Sergei Murashov (0-4-1 / .871 SV% in 5 GS) will likely start for Pittsburgh. Anaheim has two options in net: Lukáš Dostál (4-4-1 / .866 SV% in 10 GS) and Laurent Brossoit (3-0-0 / .847 SV% in 3 GS). Dostál has started four of their last ten games, including the last one on Friday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.

items.text: The Penguins have been without Trevor van Riemsdyk, Elmer Söderblom and Bryan Rust for several games.

The Ducks are newly without A.J. Greer, and have been without Troy Terry and Tyson Hinds for several games. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Mammoth are missing more right now.
Cutter Gauthier has twelve goals on chances worth about 6.6 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
Jackson LaCombe has a point in nine straight games.
